symptom: `run --local` could not start a 188-module, 12,900-document app (Mendix 10.24.26): the cold first build failed with "serve build request ... context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)" at a fixed 10 minutes, and the runtime start failed with "cannot connect to Mendix admin API at 127.0.0.1:24811 -- is the app running?" while the after-startup microflow was still running, after which mxcli shut the runtime down. Neither limit had a flag or an environment variable.
cause: ServeServer.Build used http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Minute}; StartLocalRuntime gave the M2EE connection a 150 s timeout that bounded every admin call, including `start`, which does not answer until the after-startup action returns. callM2EEDirect reported any client error, a timeout included, as an unreachable app.
file: cmd/mxcli/docker/mxserve.go (BuildTimeout, serveBuildTimeout, durationSetting), cmd/mxcli/docker/runtime_controller.go (StartTimeout, callStartPhase), cmd/mxcli/docker/m2ee.go (timeout is 'did not answer', isAdminTimeout), cmd/mxcli/cmd_run.go (--build-timeout, --start-timeout)
insight: A per-connection timeout is the wrong unit when one action on the connection is a different kind of call: `start` and `execute_ddl_commands` run user code and a schema update, every other admin action is a quick query. Give the long ones their own limit and keep the short one for the rest, so a hung status probe still fails fast. And a timeout is the server holding the request, not refusing it: reporting it as 'is the app running?' sent the user looking for a dead process in a live one. The isTimeout helper buildRetryingServeTimeout already used is the seam for both; wrap with %w so the retry still recognises the error. Control: with the limits stubbed back to 10m/150s and the timeout branch disabled, the two behaviour tests fail and the start test prints the reported 'cannot connect ... is the app running?' text.
